problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t),$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=2\pi $ and velocity $v=4$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$

feedback.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=20{t}^{3}+12,$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=-3$ and velocity $v=1$ when $t=0,$ the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$x(t)={t}^{5}+\,$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (20{t}^{3}+12)\,\text{d}t \\  & =5{t}^{4}+12t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =0+0+C \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=5{t}^{4}+12t+1.$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (5{t}^{4}+12t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{5}+6{t}^{2}+t+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K$, we use the fact that $x(0)=-3.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-3 & =0+0+0+K \\ K & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)={t}^{5}+6{t}^{2}+t-3.
$$
